issues.what: India: 679 land cells of the Indian states (Madhya Pradesh 539, Kerala 76, Rajasthan 42...) unowned on 1 January 1960 and all of 1960; the 1961 keyframe snap added 661. Cause: the Cliopatria 1956-1960 outline (republic-of-india_1956) lacks them.
Bialystok and Podlachia (93 cells) plus 13 Bug-line cells of Lublin province drawn as Byelorussian SSR for the whole window (the packet's 1969 conflict, 101 cell-years, is only the last year).
Union republics drawn mostly as the Union's own land: Ukraine 1204 of 2357 cells, Belarus 753 of 925, Lithuania 115, Moldova 111 of 129, Kirghizia 66, Kazakhstan 25.

Russian SFSR holds 3,322 of 64,533 Russian cells (a half-tint strip in the west); the rest of Russia is the Union direct. Not patched: making all of Russia a constituent would leave the Union with no cells and jump the picture at 1960 and 1970 against the windows around.
Greece: 58 cells (Crete 11, Peloponnese 11, Thrace 6, Central Greece 6, Attica 5...) unowned all window; the 1963 kingdom shape and the 1967 junta shape snap them off again (62 removed in 1967).

Okinawa drawn as plain Japan although under US administration to 15 May 1972: Japan's ledger opens the occupation in 1945 (ledger/80), but its 1952 end of the home-islands occupation (ledger/112) closes the one occupation the compiler keeps for the US-Japan pair, and the Bonin end of 1968 (ledger/114) would close it again.

Gaza province (252 cells) drawn as Estado Novo's direct land inside Portuguese Mozambique in the published draft (since the 1910 keyframe). In the trial anchor another window's patch already moves it to the colony, so my event and ruling settled nothing and were dropped.

Namibia occupation drawn with the roles reversed (owner south-africa, occupier namibia, 2,947 cells, from 1966): the compiler swaps roles when the event's author holds the cells and the counterpart (namibia, founded 1990) holds none. The hatching is right, the table is not.
Golan occupation of 1967 also reversed (owner state-of-israel, occupier syria, 2 cells); West Bank, Gaza and Sinai are right.
Sudan / UAR conflict in the Red Sea governorate (86 cells, 1961-1963): the UAR wins; the cells look like the Hala'ib triangle, which Sudan administered after 1958. Not examined (page budget).

Saudi 1969 keyframe snap adds 141 cells (Ash Sharqiyah 130, a desert patch west of Oman that is unowned 1960-1968, and 138 cells held by the Aden Protectorate inside modern Saudi Arabia until 1966-67); no ledger event explains it and no page was opened on the Rub al Khali claims.

Small size-rule conflicts and snaps that are border noise of Cliopatria's shapes: Estado Novo in Rhodesia, Malawi, Zimbabwe (22, 14), Rhodesia/Botswana (20), Kenya/Somalia (18), Congo/Zambia (19), Libya/Chad and Libya/Algeria (25, 20), Nigeria/Cameroon, british-east-africa slivers in South Africa and Namibia (1961-65).

Lake cells (Victoria, Malawi, Tanganyika) are unowned after the 1962-1964 snaps (Tanzania 214, Uganda 132, Malawi 123 removed); other unowned specks of 20-200 cells in Canada, Alaska, Indonesia, Australia are older and constant.
Darul Islam 1963 snap (South Sulawesi 180 cells direct to Negara Islam Indonesia): the ledger carries the contest 1951-1965, so the zone is contested in the draft as it should be.
Estado Novo keeps 11 Goa-edge cells (Karnataka 10, Daman 1) 1962-1966 against India (size rule) and the 1967 snap leaves them unowned; India's 1961 snap leaves 23 stray cells unowned.

problems: events/11 of the patch (US ends its occupation of Okinawa, 15 May 1972) is dated outside the window (p1970-p1979) and reaches across the boundary; it closes the relation events/9 and events/10 open. If p1970-p1979 adds its own close, one of the two is a no-op.

Root causes sit in earlier windows and my entries are insurance: the India holes come from republic-of-india_1956 (the Cliopatria 1956-1960 outline, released at the 1956 snap, so p1950-p1959 should override it); the Greek specks from kingdom-of-greece_1949 (the 1949-1962 shape); the Soviet republics' Union-direct land from the 1939-1945 transfers that went to the Union (Poland's ledger gives the land to the Union, the republics' gains find nothing). If those windows fix them first, events/0, 2, 3-8 settle nothing in the next compile and show as applied with no cell changed.

The trial's 1 January 1960 anchor already differs from the published one by 1,434 cells (other windows' patches since 1 November: Gaza to the colony, Ruanda-Urundi given its cells, 941 cells of Russia from the republic to the Union), so the packet's conflict and snap figures are partly stale; belgian-congo / ruanda-urundi shows 330 cell-years (R1) in the trial because of those patches, not mine.

Compiler: an occupation is keyed by the pair of states and *_end ignores its region, so one US-Japan end (home islands 1952, Bonin 1968) closes the Ryukyu occupation too; and occupation_start swaps the roles whenever the author holds the cells (Namibia 1966, Golan 1967), so the open_occupations table lists some owners and occupiers the wrong way round.

The greek-junta_1973 keyframe ('shape unchanged') probably carries the same 62 unowned cells at the 1973 snap in p1970-p1979; and estado-novo_1974 and 1975 keyframes may take Gaza back from the colony if the upstream fix is only an event.

Seam: the six republics' land turns constituent on 1 January 1960 (events/3-8), a visible jump from 1959 until p1950-p1959 fixes the same land; the Russian SFSR / Union split in Russia (3,322 vs 61,095 cells) is left for the orchestrator to rule on once for all Soviet windows.
Unowned lake and island specks (Great Lakes, Lake Victoria and Malawi, Arctic Canada, Alaska) run through the whole window at about 3,400 cells; they were not patched.
